figures.title: One speculative round: draft, verify, accept, emit
figures.caption: Speculative decoding drafts k tokens cheaply, then verifies all k in one batched target forward pass. Accept token i left to right with probability min(1, p_i/q_i); at the first rejection, sample from the residual max(0, p − q) and stop. The accepted prefix plus that sample is exact for the target distribution, so the output distribution is unchanged. With k = 4, α = 0.7, t_d = 0.2 t_t and t_v = 1.0 t_t, E = 2.7731 over a 1.8 t_t round, a 1.54× speedup.
figures.alt: Five lanes across five steps. The drafter proposes four tokens at cheap cost. The target scores all four positions plus a bonus position in one forward pass. The acceptance lane applies min(1, p over q) left to right, then samples the residual max(0, p minus q) at the first rejection. The KV cache lane keeps the accepted prefix, truncates the rest and keeps the bonus token. The output lane emits between one and k plus one tokens.

data.note: Exactness: a token drafted with probability q and target probability p is emitted with q·min(1, p/q) + (1 − accept)·max(0, p − q)/Z = p. Example: q = (0.5, 0.3, 0.2), p = (0.2, 0.5, 0.3); A is accepted with probability 0.4, and on rejection the residual (0, 0.2, 0.1)/0.3 samples B with 2/3 or C with 1/3. The output probabilities are 0.2, 0.5 and 0.3.

anim.intro: Press Play or Next to walk one draft-and-verify round.

steps.label: The drafter proposes k = 4 tokens, x1 to x4, at t_d each. Its own decode is bandwidth-bound too, but its weights are smaller, so it runs faster than the target.

The target scores all four positions in one forward pass. The kernel loads each weight matrix once and multiplies it by a k-row activation matrix, so weight traffic matches a one-token decode while arithmetic grows by roughly k = 4.
Accept left to right with probability min(1, p/q). A token the target believes in at least as much as the draft is always kept; otherwise it survives only part of the time.
At the first rejection, sample the residual proportional to max(0, p - q) and stop. The accepted mass and the residual mass add up to p exactly, so the output stays target-distributed.
Emit the accepted prefix plus one replacement or bonus token: between 1 and k + 1 = 5 tokens per round. Rejected drafts have their KV entries truncated to the accepted prefix length.

figures.title: Acceptance alone does not decide the speedup
figures.caption: Speedup depends on acceptance and drafter cost, not acceptance alone. With k = 4, a drafter at α = 0.7, t_d = 0.2 t_t and t_v = 1.0 t_t gives E = 2.7731 over a 1.8 t_t round, or 1.54×. A faster drafter at α = 0.3 and t_d = 0.05 t_t gives E = 1.4251 over 1.2 t_t, or 1.19×. At α = 0.1 and t_v = 1.2 t_t, E = 1.1111 over 1.24 t_t, or 0.896× — slower than not speculating.
figures.alt: Three horizontal bars, all relative to baseline target decode at 1.0. The first is 1.54 times, from acceptance 0.7 and a drafter costing 0.2 of a target step. The second is 1.19 times, from acceptance 0.3 and a drafter costing 0.05 of a target step. The third is 0.896 times, below break-even, from acceptance 0.1 and verification costing 1.2 target steps.

data.note: Each bar is the formula in the chapter: E = (1 − α^{k+1}) / (1 − α) over the round time k t_d + t_v, at k = 4. The first two bars differ only in α and t_d, so a drafter accepted less often can still lose ground even when it is cheaper. The third bar falls below 1.0 because verification costs more than the round saves.

anim.intro: Press Play or Next to price three drafters against the same verification pass.

steps.label: Expected tokens per round are E = 1 + α + α^2 + ... + α^k = (1 - α^(k+1))/(1 - α). With k = 4 and α = 0.7 that is 1 + 0.7 + 0.49 + 0.343 + 0.2401 = 2.7731.
Round time is k·t_d + t_v = 4 x 0.2 t_t + 1.0 t_t = 1.8 t_t, so speedup is 2.7731/1.8 = 1.54x.
A faster drafter at α = 0.3 and t_d = 0.05 t_t gives E = 1.4251 over a round of 4 x 0.05 t_t + 1.0 t_t = 1.2 t_t, so speedup is 1.4251/1.2 = 1.19x. It loses to the slower, higher-acceptance drafter.
At t_v = 1.2 t_t and α = 0.1, E = 1.1111 over a round of 1.24 t_t gives 0.896x. Verification costs more than the round saves, so this drafter loses to no speculation at all.

sources.note: Leviathan et al., Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding (2023): draft-then-verify and the acceptance rule.
Chen et al., Accelerating Large Language Model Decoding with Speculative Sampling (2023): the residual distribution that makes the output exact.
